passages.text: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He made a statue out of gold.
The statue was very tall.
It was sixty cubits high.
It was six cubits wide.
Nebuchadnezzar set up the statue.
He placed it on the plain of Dura.
The plain of Dura was in the province of Babylon.
passages.original: נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א עֲבַד֙ צְלֵ֣ם דִּֽי־ דְהַ֔ב רוּמֵהּ֙ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁתִּ֔ין פְּתָיֵ֖הּ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁ֑ת אֲקִימֵהּ֙ בְּבִקְעַ֣ת דּוּרָ֔א בִּמְדִינַ֖ת בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other officials of the provinces to attend the dedication of the statue he had set up.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He made a golden statue.
He set up this statue in the province of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar sent a message to all the officials in his kingdom.
He called the satraps.
He called the prefects.
He called the governors.
He called the advisers.
He called the treasurers.
He called the judges.
He called the magistrates.
He called all the other officials of the provinces.
He told them to come together.
He told them to attend the dedication of the statue he had set up.
passages.original: וּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֡א שְׁלַ֡ח לְמִכְנַ֣שׁ׀ לַֽאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֡א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּֽפַחֲוָתָ֡א אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּא֩ גְדָ֨בְרַיָּ֤א דְּתָבְרַיָּא֙ תִּפְתָּיֵ֔א וְכֹ֖ל שִׁלְטֹנֵ֣י מְדִֽינָתָ֑א לְמֵתֵא֙ לַחֲנֻכַּ֣ת צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the rulers of the provinces assembled for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He made a large golden statue.
He set up the statue on the plain of Dura in Babylon.
He called all the important officials of the provinces.
These officials included satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all other rulers.
All these officials gathered together.
They came for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
They stood in front of the statue.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֡יִן מִֽתְכַּנְּשִׁ֡ין אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֡א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּֽפַחֲוָתָ֡א אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּ֣א גְדָבְרַיָּא֩ דְּתָ֨בְרַיָּ֜א תִּפְתָּיֵ֗א וְכֹל֙ שִׁלְטֹנֵ֣י מְדִֽינָתָ֔א לַחֲנֻכַּ֣ת צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֑א וְקָאֲמִין לָקֳבֵ֣ל צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּֽר׃

passages.text: Then the herald loudly proclaimed, “O people of every nation and language, this is what you are commanded: As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He set up a golden statue.
He wanted everyone to worship this statue.
A herald spoke with a loud voice.
He spoke to all the people.
He spoke to every nation and every language.
He gave a command to everyone.
He said, “When you hear the sound of music, obey this command.
You will hear the horn.
You will hear the flute.
You will hear the zither.
You will hear the lyre.
You will hear the harp.
You will hear the pipes.
You will hear all kinds of music.
When you hear these sounds, you must fall down.
You must worship the golden statue.
King Nebuchadnezzar set up this statue.”
passages.original: וְכָרוֹזָ֖א קָרֵ֣א בְחָ֑יִל לְכ֤וֹן אָֽמְרִין֙ עַֽמְמַיָּ֔א אֻמַּיָּ֖א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּֽא׃ בְּעִדָּנָ֡א דִּֽי־ תִשְׁמְע֡וּן קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַ֠שְׁרוֹקִיתָא קִיתָרוֹס סַבְּכָ֤א פְּסַנְתֵּרִין֙ סוּמְפֹּ֣נְיָ֔ה וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א תִּפְּל֤וּן וְתִסְגְּדוּן֙ לְצֶ֣לֶם דַּהֲבָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: And whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar gave a command.
He set up a golden statue.
He ordered everyone to worship the statue.
He said, “Whoever does not fall down and worship the statue will be punished.”
That person will be thrown at once into a blazing fiery furnace.
passages.original: וּמַן־ דִּי־ לָ֥א יִפֵּ֖ל וְיִסְגֻּ֑ד בַּהּ־ שַׁעֲתָ֣א יִתְרְמֵ֔א לְגֽוֹא־ אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore, as soon as all the people heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and all kinds of music, the people of every nation and language would fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He set up a golden statue.
He commanded all people to worship this statue.
People from every nation and language lived in his kingdom.
Musicians played the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and many other instruments.
Whenever the people heard the sound of the music, they obeyed the king’s command.
All the people from every nation and language fell down.
They worshiped the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֡ה בֵּהּ־ זִמְנָ֡א כְּדִ֣י שָֽׁמְעִ֣ין כָּֽל־ עַמְמַיָּ֡א קָ֣ל קַרְנָא֩ מַשְׁר֨וֹקִיתָ֜א קִיתָרֹס שַׂבְּכָא֙ פְּסַנְטֵרִ֔ין וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א נָֽפְלִ֨ין כָּֽל־ עַֽמְמַיָּ֜א אֻמַיָּ֣א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֗א סָֽגְדִין֙ לְצֶ֣לֶם דַּהֲבָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: At this time some astrologers came forward and maliciously accused the Jews, saying to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, may you live forever!
passages.sermon:
Some astrologers lived in Babylon.
These astrologers were called Chaldeans.
At that time, the Chaldeans came forward.
They accused the Jews.
They spoke against the Jews with hostility.
They went to King Nebuchadnezzar.
They spoke to the king.
They said, “O king, may you live forever.”
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֤ל דְּנָה֙ בֵּהּ־ זִמְנָ֔א קְרִ֖בוּ גֻּבְרִ֣ין כַּשְׂדָּאִ֑ין וַאֲכַ֥לוּ קַרְצֵיה֖וֹן דִּ֥י יְהוּדָיֵֽא׃ עֲנוֹ֙ וְאָ֣מְרִ֔ין לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּ֑א מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃

passages.text: You, O king, have issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music must fall down and worship the golden statue, and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar made a law.
He commanded all people to obey this law.
The law says: When anyone hears the sound of music, they must act.
The music includes the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of instruments.
When people hear this music, they must fall down.
They must worship the golden statue.
King Nebuchadnezzar set up this statue.
Anyone who does not fall down and worship will be punished.
The punishment is this: They will be thrown into a blazing fiery furnace.
passages.original: אַנְתָּה מַלְכָּא֮ שָׂ֣מְתָּ טְּעֵם֒ דִּ֣י כָל־ אֱנָ֡שׁ דִּֽי־ יִשְׁמַ֡ע קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַ֠שְׁרֹקִיתָא קִיתָרֹס שַׂבְּכָ֤א פְסַנְתֵּרִין֙ וְסִיפֹּנְיָה וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א יִפֵּ֥ל וְיִסְגֻּ֖ד לְצֶ֥לֶם דַּהֲבָֽא׃ וּמַן־ דִּי־ לָ֥א יִפֵּ֖ל וְיִסְגֻּ֑ד יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְגֽוֹא־ אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃

passages.text: But there are some Jews you have appointed to manage the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have ignored you, O king, and have refused to serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are Jews.
You, O king, appointed them to manage the province of Babylon.
These men do not obey you, O king.
They do not serve your gods.
They do not worship the golden statue you have set up.
passages.original: אִיתַ֞י גֻּבְרִ֣ין יְהוּדָאיִ֗ן דִּֽי־ מַנִּ֤יתָ יָתְהוֹן֙ עַל־ עֲבִידַת֙ מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֔ל שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ לָא־ שָׂ֨מֽוּ עֲלַיִךְ מַלְכָּא֙ טְעֵ֔ם לֵאלָהַיִךְ לָ֣א פָלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימְתָּ לָ֥א סָגְדִֽין׃ס

passages.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar, furious with rage, summoned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king, and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden statue I have set up?
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He became very angry.
He was filled with rage.
He called for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
These three men were Jews.
The king had appointed them to manage the province of Babylon.
The king ordered them to come before him.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego stood before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke to them.
He said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true?
You do not serve my gods.
You do not worship the golden statue I have set up.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֤יִן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר֙ בִּרְגַ֣ז וַחֲמָ֔ה אֲמַר֙ לְהַיְתָיָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ הֵיתָ֖יוּ קֳדָ֥ם מַלְכָּֽא׃ עָנֵ֤ה נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְה֔וֹן הַצְדָּ֕א שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לֵֽאלָהַ֗י לָ֤א אִֽיתֵיכוֹן֙ פָּֽלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימֶת לָ֥א סָֽגְדִֽין׃

passages.text: Now, if you are ready, as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the statue I have made. But if you refuse to worship, you will be thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace. Then what god will be able to deliver you from my hands?”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He ruled Babylon.
He had set up a golden statue.
He commanded everyone to worship this statue.
He said, “If you are ready, listen carefully.
When you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down.
You must worship the statue I have made.
If you do not worship, you will be thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace.
No god will be able to deliver you from my hands.”
passages.original: כְּעַ֞ן הֵ֧ן אִֽיתֵיכ֣וֹן עֲתִידִ֗ין דִּ֣י בְעִדָּנָ֡א דִּֽי־ תִשְׁמְע֡וּן קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַשְׁרוֹקִיתָ֣א קִיתָרֹס שַׂבְּכָ֡א פְּסַנְתֵּרִין֩ וְסוּמְפֹּ֨נְיָ֜ה וְכֹ֣ל׀ זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֗א תִּפְּל֣וּן וְתִסְגְּדוּן֮ לְצַלְמָ֣א דִֽי־ עַבְדֵת֒ וְהֵן֙ לָ֣א תִסְגְּד֔וּן בַּהּ־ שַׁעֲתָ֣ה תִתְרְמ֔וֹן לְגֽוֹא־ אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּ֑א וּמַן־ ה֣וּא אֱלָ֔הּ דֵּ֥י יְשֵֽׁיזְבִנְכ֖וֹן מִן־ יְדָֽי׃

passages.text: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were three Jewish men.
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar questioned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He asked them about their refusal to worship his gods and the golden statue.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to Nebuchadnezzar.
They said, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves to you about this matter.”
passages.original: עֲנ֗וֹ שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ וְאָמְרִ֖ין לְמַלְכָּ֑א נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר לָֽא־ חַשְׁחִ֨ין אֲנַ֧חְנָה עַל־ דְּנָ֛ה פִּתְגָ֖ם לַהֲתָבוּתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego served the God of Israel.
They spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
They said their God is able to save them.
Their God can rescue them from the blazing fiery furnace.
Their God can also deliver them from the king’s hand.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן אִיתַ֗י אֱלָהַ֙נָא֙ דִּֽי־ אֲנַ֣חְנָא פָֽלְחִ֔ין יָכִ֖ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתַ֑נָא מִן־ אַתּ֨וּן נוּרָ֧א יָקִֽדְתָּ֛א וּמִן־ יְדָ֥ךְ מַלְכָּ֖א יְשֵׁיזִֽב׃

passages.text: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
They were faithful Jews.
They refused to worship other gods.
They said, "Even if our God does not save us, know this, O king."
"We will not serve your gods."
"We will not worship the golden statue you have set up."
passages.original: וְהֵ֣ן לָ֔א יְדִ֥יעַ לֶהֱוֵא־ לָ֖ךְ מַלְכָּ֑א דִּ֤י לֵֽאלָהָיִךְ֙ לָא־ אִיתַיְנָא פָֽלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימְתָּ לָ֥א נִסְגֻּֽד׃ס

passages.text: At this, Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and the expression on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual, and he commanded some mighty men of valor in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king.
He became very angry.
His face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He gave an order.
He told his servants to heat the furnace.
He wanted the furnace seven times hotter than usual.
He called for strong soldiers from his army.
He told the soldiers to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He commanded them to throw these three men into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֨יִן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר הִתְמְלִ֣י חֱמָ֗א וּצְלֵ֤ם אַנְפּ֙וֹהִי֙ אֶשְׁתַּנּוּ עַל־ שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ עָנֵ֤ה וְאָמַר֙ לְמֵזֵ֣א לְאַתּוּנָ֔א חַ֨ד־ שִׁבְעָ֔ה עַ֛ל דִּ֥י חֲזֵ֖ה לְמֵזְיֵֽהּ׃ וּלְגֻבְרִ֤ין גִּבָּֽרֵי־ חַ֙יִל֙ דִּ֣י בְחַיְלֵ֔הּ אֲמַר֙ לְכַפָּתָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לְמִרְמֵ֕א לְאַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃

passages.text: So they were tied up, wearing robes, trousers, turbans, and other clothes, and they were thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were three men.
Soldiers tied them up tightly.
They wore their robes.
They wore their trousers.
They wore their turbans.
They wore their other clothes.
The soldiers threw them into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֜יִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ כְּפִ֙תוּ֙ בְּסַרְבָּלֵיהוֹן֙ פַּטִּישֵׁיהוֹן וְכַרְבְּלָתְה֖וֹן וּלְבֻשֵׁיה֑וֹן וּרְמִ֕יו לְגֽוֹא־ אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃

passages.text: The king’s command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the fiery flames killed the men who carried up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar gave a very urgent command.
The furnace was extremely hot.
Some men carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to the furnace.
The fiery flames killed these men.
The flames killed them because the furnace was so hot.
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֗ה מִן־ דִּ֞י מִלַּ֤ת מַלְכָּא֙ מַחְצְפָ֔ה וְאַתּוּנָ֖א אֵזֵ֣ה יַתִּ֑ירָא גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ דִּ֤י הַסִּ֙קוּ֙ לְשַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ קַטִּ֣ל הִמּ֔וֹן שְׁבִיבָ֖א דִּ֥י נוּרָֽא׃

passages.text: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, firmly bound, fell into the blazing fiery furnace.
passages.sermon:
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were three men.
They were firmly tied up.
People threw them into a blazing, fiery furnace.
They fell into the fire while still bound.
passages.original: וְגֻבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ תְּלָ֣תֵּה֔וֹן שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ נְפַ֛לוּ לְגֽוֹא־ אַתּוּן־ נוּרָ֥א יָֽקִדְתָּ֖א מְכַפְּתִֽין׃פ

passages.text: Suddenly King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up in amazement and asked his advisers, “Did we not throw three men, firmly bound, into the fire?” “Certainly, O king,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He saw something that amazed him.
He stood up quickly.
He was alarmed.
He spoke to his advisers.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Did we not throw three men into the fire?”
He reminded them that the men were firmly bound.
The advisers answered the king.
They said, “Certainly, O king.”
passages.original: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֔א תְּוַ֖הּ וְקָ֣ם בְּהִתְבְּהָלָ֑ה עָנֵ֨ה וְאָמַ֜ר לְהַדָּֽבְר֗וֹהִי הֲלָא֩ גֻבְרִ֨ין תְּלָתָ֜א רְמֵ֤ינָא לְגוֹא־ נוּרָא֙ מְכַפְּתִ֔ין עָנַ֤יִן וְאָמְרִין֙ לְמַלְכָּ֔א יַצִּיבָ֖א מַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: “Look!” he exclaimed. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire—and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar saw something amazing.
He looked into the blazing fiery furnace.
He saw four men inside the fire.
All four men walked around freely.
None of them were tied up.
None of them were hurt by the fire.
The fourth man looked different.
The fourth man looked like a son of the gods.
passages.original: עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר הָֽא־ אֲנָ֨ה חָזֵ֜ה גֻּבְרִ֣ין אַרְבְּעָ֗ה שְׁרַ֙יִן֙ מַהְלְכִ֣ין בְּגֽוֹא־ נוּרָ֔א וַחֲבָ֖ל לָא־ אִיתַ֣י בְּה֑וֹן וְרֵוֵהּ֙ דִּ֣י רְבִיעָיָא דָּמֵ֖ה לְבַר־ אֱלָהִֽין׃ס

passages.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the blazing fiery furnace and called out, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!” So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fire, and when the satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers had gathered around, they saw that the fire had no effect on the bodies of these men. Not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of fire on them.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He went to the door of the blazing fiery furnace.
He called out to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fire.
The satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers gathered around them.
They looked at these men.
They saw that the fire had no effect on their bodies.
Not a hair on their heads was singed.
Their robes were not harmed.
There was no smell of fire on them.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֜יִן קְרֵ֣ב נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר לִתְרַע֮ אַתּ֣וּן נוּרָ֣א יָקִֽדְתָּא֒ עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר שַׁדְרַ֨ךְ מֵישַׁ֧ךְ וַעֲבֵד־ נְג֛וֹ עַבְד֛וֹהִי דִּֽי־ אֱלָהָ֥א עִלָּיָא פֻּ֣קוּ וֶאֱת֑וֹ בֵּאדַ֣יִן נָֽפְקִ֗ין שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֛ךְ וַעֲבֵ֥ד נְג֖וֹ מִן־ גּ֥וֹא נוּרָֽא׃ וּ֠מִֽתְכַּנְּשִׁין אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֞א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָא֮ וְהַדָּבְרֵ֣י מַלְכָּא֒ חָזַ֣יִן לְגֻבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֡ךְ דִּי֩ לָֽא־ שְׁלֵ֨ט נוּרָ֜א בְּגֶשְׁמְה֗וֹן וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵֽאשְׁהוֹן֙ לָ֣א הִתְחָרַ֔ךְ וְסָרְבָּלֵיה֖וֹן לָ֣א שְׁנ֑וֹ וְרֵ֣יחַ נ֔וּר לָ֥א עֲדָ֖ת בְּהֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Nebuchadnezzar declared, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him. They violated the king’s command and risked their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke.
He praised the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He said, “Blessed be their God.
This God sent His angel.
He rescued His servants.
These men trusted in their God.
They disobeyed the king’s command.
They gave up their lives.
They chose not to serve any other god.
They chose not to worship any god except their own God.”
passages.original: עָנֵ֨ה נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר וְאָמַ֗ר בְּרִ֤יךְ אֱלָהֲהוֹן֙ דִּֽי־ שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ דִּֽי־ שְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאֲכֵהּ֙ וְשֵׁיזִ֣ב לְעַבְד֔וֹהִי דִּ֥י הִתְרְחִ֖צוּ עֲל֑וֹהִי וּמִלַּ֤ת מַלְכָּא֙ שַׁנִּ֔יו וִיהַ֣בוּ גֶשְׁמֵיהוֹן דִּ֠י לָֽא־ יִפְלְח֤וּן וְלָֽא־ יִסְגְּדוּן֙ לְכָל־ אֱלָ֔הּ לָהֵ֖ן לֵאלָֽהֲהֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. For there is no other god who can deliver in this way.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar made a decree.
He ruled over Babylon.
He spoke to all people, nations, and languages.
He said, “If anyone says anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, they will be cut into pieces.
Their houses will be turned into rubble.
No other god can save like this God.”
passages.original: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּי֩ כָל־ עַ֨ם אֻמָּ֜ה וְלִשָּׁ֗ן דִּֽי־ יֵאמַ֤ר שֵׁלָה עַ֣ל אֱלָהֲה֗וֹן דִּֽי־ שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹא הַדָּמִ֣ין יִתְעֲבֵ֔ד וּבַיְתֵ֖הּ נְוָלִ֣י יִשְׁתַּוֵּ֑ה כָּל־ קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֣י לָ֤א אִיתַי֙ אֱלָ֣ה אָחֳרָ֔ן דִּֽי־ יִכֻּ֥ל לְהַצָּלָ֖ה כִּדְנָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He saw that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego trusted God.
He saw that God saved them from danger.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
He gave them higher positions in the province of Babylon.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֗א הַצְלַ֛ח לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֛ךְ וַעֲבֵ֥ד נְג֖וֹ בִּמְדִינַ֥ת בָּבֶֽל׃פ
